title: Sharp Treatment Effect Intervals from Two-Replicate Pooled Testing with Call Errors
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The note proves sharp arm-risk and ATE intervals, but much of their identification logic specializes the established finite misclassification framework of Molinari (2008) and classical edge-cover results.
Its resource-optimal design result is conditional on high-girth feasibility or confined to boundary values; the intermediate positive-excess frontier remains open.
The low-prevalence reversal ranks Petersen against one prism, not optimal expected-width designs across the resource class.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier subfield is capped at incremental.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and independently audited sharp attainable arm-risk and ATE intervals, an exact mean-budget concave-envelope theorem, matching-versus-hardness results, matrix-pooling compression, finite girth optima, and a fourth-order Petersen/prism reversal. Mathematical and citation review passed, but the field gate capped the package at incremental because central identification steps specialize prior misclassification and edge-cover theory, the general intermediate design-excess frontier remains open, and the expected-width comparison is not class-optimal. A higher-tier successor would need a genuinely new class-wide result such as exact Delta_{M,N,4} across feasible resources or global expected-width optimization, not a reframing of this note.
tldr: Two-replicate Boolean pool graphs yield sharp arm-risk and treatment-effect intervals under separately stated local call-error caps or arm-average budgets. For all-negative observations, high girth attains the local-cap benchmark when resource feasible; the mean-budget frontier instead follows a concave envelope and regular graphs tie. The resource-constrained excess now has exact feasibility and boundary formulas: in particular \(\Delta_{M,N,M-1}=N-\lfloor2N/M\rfloor-M+2\), attained exactly by admissible graphs of maximum possible minimum degree. Intermediate positive-excess designs remain open. Petersen improves two local minimax criteria over the pentagonal prism, whereas the prism has smaller fixed-graph expected width at sufficiently small positive prevalence.
gap: Generic sharp direct-misclassification regions and compatible defective-set combinatorics are established. The inspected theorem text does not provide explicit finite two-replicate graph envelopes lifted arm by arm to a cluster-randomized ATE, nor the all-negative hard-local-cap and unrestricted-completion two-infection design frontiers. This is a bounded priority assessment, with count-estimation full-text access a remaining limit.
fill: Derive the graph-specific envelopes and causal-law witnesses under separate local and arm-average error regimes, certify complete-bipartite compression, and establish the two finite girth criteria with their average-budget and expected-width limitations.
